en.html:
A fire without warning: there was nothing more frightening. The moment the alarm rang, the whole neighbourhood lost its sleep. People came rushing into the street.

And naturally, they saw.

The half-built bridge, now approaching completion.
Four men moving about it.

The tools in their hands. A saw, a machete, a hatchet...

And their faces. Nowhere to run, and no useful thought arriving to replace running.

en.html:
Four gangsters accustomed to violence, and me with empty hands. Not an arrangement in my favour. A tsurugi, however, would be excessive. One sword would do. No need to bring an armoured warrior to a neighbourhood argument. The bridge had suffered enough already.

I had to give them credit: even if the sudden appearance of a sword in my hand startled them, they offered no opening. Two came forward; the other two moved around to my left and right.

Four against one. The proper move was to put some distance between us and avoid being surrounded.

But not this time. I could not afford a lengthy affair. If they turned those blades on the people around us, it would be a disaster. The public had come out to watch; I could not let the demonstration start including them.

Resident or refugee, I would not let them hurt anyone.

So, no retreat. Forward.

Toward the man with the machete, ahead and to my right—

I let out a breath and wiped away the sweat. The fighting had been short and fierce; it had taken a great deal out of both body and mind.

By a narrow margin, I was unhurt. All four gangsters lay on the ground, but none of them had a life-threatening wound either.

...A good result, I supposed. Though not having to fight would have been better than a good result from fighting.

At her answer, I let the tension go out of my body. Whatever else, this matter was settled.

I did not expect residents and refugees to put their arms around each other and start laughing straightaway. Still, their relations would surely improve. One root of the conflict had been removed.

The people around me, watching...

In that instant, the air boiled.

When the gangsters drew their weapons, it had been nothing like this. Hoarse cries escaped from mouth after mouth. People leapt back as though away from a fire, making a wide space around me.

Farther away. A little farther. And when the people behind them left no room, they got in each other's way and began cursing.
